record.paper_title: Towards Knowledge Exchange: State-of-the-Art and Open Problems
record.original_question: If positive or negative examples are available for a knowledge-base mapping task, can rule-mining methods identify important paths or rules and enrich the source or target ontologies with induced constraints in a way that helps generate better mapping rules?

evidence.quote: It is interesting to see whether enriching the source/target ontologies with additional induced constraints produced by running a rule mining algorithm can help generate better mapping rules.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let S and T be two ontologies, each given as a set of logical axioms over a signature of classes, properties, and individuals, and let a mapping between S and T be a finite set M of rules of the form φ(x) → ψ(x), where φ is a conjunctive query over S and ψ a conjunctive query over T. Suppose one is given a finite collection of positive examples E⁺ ⊆ S × T (pairs of entities that should be linked by the mapping) and negative examples E⁻ ⊆ S × T (pairs that should not). A rule-mining algorithm A takes as input an ontology O together with a set of instance data and outputs a finite set of Horn rules (constraints) C(O) such that O ∪ C(O) remains consistent and each rule in C(O) has support and confidence above prescribed thresholds with respect to the instance data.

Question: Does there exist a rule-mining procedure A and a mapping-induction procedure F such that, for a suitable class of ontology pairs (S, T) and examples (E⁺, E⁻), the mapping
   F(S ∪ C(S), T ∪ C(T), E⁺, E⁻)
is provably superior — with respect to a fixed evaluation measure such as F-score on a held-out test set of correct correspondences — to the mapping F(S, T, E⁺, E⁻) obtained without enriching the ontologies by induced constraints? Equivalently, characterize conditions on (S, T, E⁺, E⁻) under which enrichment by mined rules strictly improves the quality of induced mapping rules, and identify a class where such improvement is impossible.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open research direction concerning whether rule-mining-induced ontology constraints can systematically improve ontology mapping when positive/negative examples are available. We found no published result that formally settles this question; related work on AMIE-style rule mining and ontology alignment exists but does not provide a definitive theoretical or empirical resolution.

status_evidence.title: Towards Knowledge Exchange: State-of-the-Art and Open Problems (zbMATH listing)
status_evidence.snippet: Listed as a survey-style paper outlining open problems on knowledge exchange and ontology mapping.
status_evidence.claim: The question is identified as an open research direction rather than a settled result.
